question.problem:
The intersection of the planes $x+y-1=0$ and $x+z+1=0$ is given by the line

$$
r(t)=⟨0,{a}_{2},{a}_{3}⟩+tb,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Calculate ${a}_{2}+{a}_{3},$ and find a possible direction vector $b.$
question.worked_solution:
We're given that there exists a point on the line where $x=0.$ Substituting this to the first equation gives

$$
0+y-1=0\,⟹\,y=1,
$$

and substituting $x=0$ into the second equation gives

$$
0+z+1=0\,⟹\,z=-1.
$$

Therefore, $a=⟨0,1,-1⟩$ is a position vector of a point on the line.

Next, we notice:

- For the plane $x+y-1=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨1,1,0⟩.$

- For the plane $x+z+1=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨1,0,1⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩\times ⟨1,0,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =i-j-k \\  & =⟨1,-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The equation of the line is:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+tb \\ r(t) & =⟨0,1,-1⟩+t⟨1,-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally then, ${a}_{2}+{a}_{3}=1+(-1)=0,$ and $b=⟨1,-1,-1⟩.$
